title: A 12.8GS/s Sub-Sampling ADC Front-End With 38GHz Input Bandwidth and >39dB SNDR for 1 to 32GHz in 22nm FDSOI
problem: RF-sampling ADCs for millimeter-wave receivers require simultaneous wide input bandwidth (>30GHz), high signal fidelity, and multi-band flexibility; existing implementations struggle balancing sampling aperture, aliasing rejection, and noise at RF frequencies.
motivation: mm-wave X-band to Ka-band (27–31GHz) Earth-to-Satellite communications demand high-throughput RF-sampling receivers with minimal system complexity and data-rate overhead.
method: A 12.8GS/s sub-sampling ADC front-end achieves 38GHz input bandwidth via optimized sampling aperture and anti-aliasing filtering, provides 6.4GHz Nyquist bandwidth for flexible multi-channel reception across 1–32GHz, and maintains >39dB SNDR using FDSOI technology advantages.
key_novelty: 38GHz input bandwidth RF-sampling front-end with 6.4GHz Nyquist bandwidth enabling flexible multi-channel reception across wide RF range.
contributions: 38GHz input bandwidth RF-sampling front-end for direct mm-wave digitization
6.4GHz Nyquist bandwidth enabling multi-channel reception and signal processing flexibility
Sub-sampling architecture reducing data-rate overhead vs. full Nyquist sampling
>39dB SNDR across 1–32GHz demonstrating robustness to aliasing and interference
limitations: Power consumption, jitter performance, and phase-noise characteristics not discussed.
primary_theme: 12.8GS/s RF-sampling ADC front-end with 38GHz bandwidth for mm-wave Earth-to-Satellite communications
